agree.reason: The wary backer will appreciate the open cost breakdown, the refusal to call the game a hit and the monthly-update promise, but with no delivery date and no real risks section, someone who lost $85 on a project that never shipped may still hold back.

honest.reason: It rightly declines the 'proven hit' claim, but it invents several things: convention players 'who had never heard of it', the BoardGameGeek name, a fees label for the leftover $5,450, and a promise of monthly updates. 'If fewer than half of them back the game, we still make it' also overstates, because the goal actually needs about 46% of the 1,240 sign-ups.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out 572 backers and $5,150 shipping for those backers, and checks the backer count against the 1,240 sign-ups. But it never shows the per-copy margin ($11.60 + $9 against $49), never says what happens to the 928 extra copies, and never states the 46% conversion the goal needs as an exact figure.

right_comparison.reason: The not-funded outcome is stated accurately (no one is charged, no print run), but the comparison leans on emotion rather than on what the facts show.

qualification.reason: The buffer 'in case costs change' gives no amount the reader can check, no date and no consequence, and there is no delivery timeline or contingency if the factory quote or shipping cost rises.

objections.reason: It names and addresses the first-time-creator worry with prepared costs and a promise of updates, but leaves out what this reader checks most: a delivery estimate, manufacturing risks and international shipping.

fit.reason: It is a crowdfunding pitch of roughly 500 words, as asked, though it still contains a '[your name]' placeholder and quietly turns down the brief's 'proven hit' framing.
